lead: `parent::Name` in a type position does not parse, so a `reject` case naming it pins a twenty-error cascade rather than the refusal it meant to.
body: The type grammar takes `Owner::Name` and a bare `Name`; `parent::` is neither, so the parser stops at the `::` and re-reads the rest of the method as class members, each with its own diagnostic. Assert what a subclass's *own* name gives — `Sub::Id` is `E0405` — and leave `parent::`/`self::`/`static::` to a case about the type grammar itself.
